text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired (P1) for service=inference-router-prod region=eu-west-1, symptom=5xx-rate spike, alert_group=router-5xx-threshold

pagerbot: PagerDuty incident INC1758211111 created. Escalation policy: oncall-inference-eu -> oncall-inference-us.

sam: taking initial ack — i'm oncall-eu, looking now. what's the customer impact?

leena: I'm seeing increased 502/504 from the router logs, ~2.4% error rate over 5m, started ~11:02 UTC. Affected route: /v1/generate (heavy batching).

alex: any rollouts around that time? CI shows a restart of router fleet at 10:58 but that was a canary, not full.

maria: Confirmed: a canary of router v2.3.1 was pushed 10:56 and rolled back at 11:03 by deploy-bot due to health checks. Might be related.

sam: grabbing logs: ```kubectl logs -n inference router-xyz --since=15m | grep ERROR | head -n 50``` shows `kv cache miss flood` + `shard mapping timeout` in the stack traces.

jordan: tagging infra: @ops-lead we might have a kvcache eviction storm + autoscaler flapping. Can you check GPU pool scaling and redis latency?

ops-lead: looking at infra: redis (kvcache) p99 latency spiked to 450ms at 11:01 in eu-west-1, nodes reported OOM-kill on one shard at 11:02, autoscaler started 3 extra router pods which momentarily increased pressure.

leena: customer impact note for page: inference requests to some EU tenants are seeing 4–8s extra latency and 502s intermittently. No broad data loss reported but degraded UX.

sam: mitigation plan proposal: 1) pin router traffic to fallback model variant (lower mem) for high-traffic tenants 2) scale kvcache read-replicas + restart the evicted redis shard 3) pause canary rollout until stability. Which should we do first?

maria: I can pause the canary — paused now via deploy console. :white_check_mark:

alex: +1 on fallback routing. I can flip the routing flag `router.use_fallback_variant=true` for affected routes. Doing gradual switch for top 10% traffic.

pagerbot: change request queued: `/opsctl feature-flip router.use_fallback_variant true --scope /v1/generate --percent 10` (run by alex). Please confirm when done.

alex: ran command, rollout started. Logs show fallback variant serving; error rate dropped to 0.9% within 90s.

leena: confirming metrics: 5xx down from 2.4% -> 0.8% over last 3m. Latency still slightly elevated p95 ~700ms but trending down.

sam: ops-lead — can we stabilize kvcache? what's ETA on redis shard restart?

ops-lead: restarted the evicted node and rejoined cluster at 11:12, replication catch-up in progress. Estimated 6–8 mins to p99 normal. I've also added one read-replica.

jordan: customer comms: recommend we ping top affected customers with note that we saw a brief 5xx spike, mitigation applied, monitoring stable. Sam can you draft?

sam: drafting now — will post to #customer-updates and queue for CS review.

maria: can we keep this incident in watch for next 30m then close if stable?

leena: agreed, keeping watch. I'll post another status ping in 10m.

pagerbot: INC1758211111 status: acknowledged -> investigating. Assigned to: sam (oncall-eu). Escalation suspended.

incident-bot: automated note: if error rate recovers below 0.5% for 30m, this incident will auto-resolve.

sam: STATUS — mitigation applied (fallback routing + paused canary + redis restart). Error rate improved. Monitoring for 30m.

alex: FYI I left a small diagnostic snippet in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/INC1758211111 (logs, graphs, commands run).

jordan: thumbs :thumbsup: good job team. I'll coordinate customer comms with CS.

leena: 10m status update: error rate stable ~0.6%, redis replication healthy, no further OOMs.

sam: 30m status update: metrics stable, moving to postmortem prep. Assigning owner for postmortem: sam + infra (ops-lead) + deploy (maria).

pagerbot: INC1758211111 marked for postmortem owner: sam, ops-lead, maria.

sam: closing note: will open follow-up runbook PR to add guidance for kvcache eviction storms and a preflight check for canaries during kv pressure. Closing thread in 1h unless re-opened. :v:
